judged_text: config/routes.rb:47-49 — `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared directly inside `resources :groups do ... end` (not inside a `member do ... end` block), so Rails does not generate `/admin/groups/:id/members`; the routes compile to the fixed path `/admin/groups/members` with no `:id`/`:group_id` segment, forcing `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`/`#remove_member` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:614-654) to trust `params.require(:group_id)` from the request body/query as the sole way to identify the target group — any other route or nested resource under `/admin/groups/:id/...` that later needs `members` will collide with this global path, and the API shape (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/members?group_id=`) is inconsistent with every other admin group action in the same file that reads `params[:id]` from the URL. Confidence 90, severity P2.

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the `delete "members"` and `put "members"` lines are nested inside `resources :groups do ... end`. In Rails, a bare route declared inside a `resources` block is a member-scoped route by default (i.e., it includes the resource identifier segment, typically `:group_id`), not a fixed collection route like `/admin/groups/members`. This matches the controller implementations in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb which do `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` for `add_members`/`remove_member`, consistent with the route segment rather than “trusting only request body/query”. The claimed collision with a global `/admin/groups/members` path is not supported by what the diff shows.
